findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were various cooked food that lacked date marking inside of the prep cooler. These items were cooked noodles and cooked chicken. Discussed with the PIC and the items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that time/temperature control (TCS) foods are date marked with the date of preparation if being held for longer than 24 hours in house.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ventilation system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles every Saturday, however, the baffles were black in color and will need to be cleaned more frequently due to the amount of frying in the facility. The ansul system was also accumulated in grease debris. See that a professional hood cleaning company services the duct work of the hood system.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the handwashing sink inside of the only functional bathroom. The PIC mentioned that the facility is aware of the issue and a plumber will be to service the sink soon. Ensure that all handsinks are equipped with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026 to check for running hot water.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There is massive leak at the handwashing sink across from the cookline. Waste water is spilling onto the floor from the pipe underneath the basin. The facility is aware of the leak and will have a plumber service the sink soon. Ensure that all piping of handsinks are in good repair and never in leaking condition. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility could benefit from a detail cleaning. Floors and walls throughout the kitchen are coated with dried grease and debris. During slow periods, be sure to pull equipment from wall to sweep, mop, and scrub accumulated areas. The inner surfaces inside of the drawer cooler were observed with spilled liquids and debris. Shown it the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as possible to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager upon beginning of the inspection. Facility has multiple CFPM’s per paperwork. Ensure there is a CFPM present during all operational hours. CFPM came during the inspection and was able to answer all paperwork related questions. COS.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements for the facility. CFPM was not aware of the document. Employee handbook for facility (chain establishment) does not contain reportable diseases section per what the Inspector witnessed. Provided copy for the facility (SCDPH document). Ensure all employees read and sign the document. Ensure all new hires read and sign the document. Keep copies in the manager’s office. Inspector will follow-up on 3/12/24.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy for the facility. CFPM was unaware of the policy. Discussed policy with PIC. Provided copy. Ensure facility has bleach to perform the procedure. A biohazard kit that kills for Norovirus will also suffice. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed two employees to improperly wash hands. No barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles after properly washing hands with water and soap. Discussed proper hand washing with CFPM. Ensure staff are properly trained. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/5/24. Staff has limited knowledge in properly hand washing based on the last inspection and today’s inspection. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off the faucet hands (such as a paper towel) to prevent cross contamination. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen training not completed by the CFPM. Provided educational handout on how to complete the awareness training. Ensure all CFPM’s complete this training. Print copies of the license. Valid for 3 years. Correct by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Facility has several priority/priority foundation violations along with a potential foodborne illness complaint. Due to the risks associated with failure to adjust practices to conform with 2017 FDA Food Code, an additional follow-up inspection is scheduled for 2/8/2024 to evaluate overall conditions at the facility.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple employees washing hands improperly and at incorrect frequencies. x2 employees failed to wash hands at glove changes. x2 employees failed to wash hands after touching potentially contaminated items including soiled potentially contaminated utensils and food timer buttons which are not cleaned nor sanitized. x2 employees washed hands without using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Inspector discussed these violations with operator who requested inspector provide additional education to staff regarding proper hand washing. Inspector showed all staff present proper hand washing technique and watched to confirm understanding. Inspector also discussed proper frequency with all staff to ensure that hands are washed any time contamination may have occurred. Inspector further discussed with operator the need to have internal processes in place to train current AND new staff on proper hand washing procedure and frequency. Additionally, inspector discussed the risk of failure to properly wash hands including the spread of foodborne illnesses to consumers and staff. Operator states understanding. A staff member on site today was instructed to ensure that other staff members are washing hands properly and communicating proper procedure. A follow-up is issued for 3-days to ensure compliance and further investigate potentially hazardous practices in relation to hand washing. Inspector will return on Thursday 1/11/2024.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
On arrival, inspector observed the easternmost hand sink in the kitchen to be blocked by a staff member working with food on a small cart. Although the cart itself was not blocking the sink, the employee utilizing the cart was blocking access. If food is to be prepared in this location to be put on the grill, food preparation must not interfere with employee ability to wash hands at ANY TIME. Ensure that all hand sinks remain accessible and unblocked at all times. A follow-up is issued for 1/18/2024 to ensure that hand sinks remain accessible at all times. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two instances of potential food contamination in the facility:
1) a container of raw beef stored on a shelf with cooked and cooled noodles
2) a container of raw chicken on the rack near the easternmost hand sink in the kitchen is exposed to splash from the nearby hand sink. Inspector observed such splash occur during handwashing following the educational demonstration provided to staff. 

Food must be protected from cross-contamination at ALL times. Ensure that proper storage order is followed in coolers with raw product stored separate from cooked product AND that foods are never stored in locations subject to splash from sinks.

Inspector will return on Thursday 1/11/2024 to ensure compliance with food protection requirements. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
An employee was observed placing soiled and potentially contaminated items including laminated sheets of paper hanging on the nearby wall and a dry erase marker directly on the food-contact surfaces of a cleaned and sanitized cutting board which the employee had just brought up to and placed on the prep counter to the right of the prep coolers. Food-contact surfaces must NEVER contact contaminated items. Logs and markers are not cleaned and sanitized items and are a source of contamination. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are protected from cross-contamination at all times. Inspector discussed this violation with operator and person-in-charge and had the contaminated cutting board and utensils removed from service to be cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up is issued for 1/11/2024 to ensure compliance with food-contact surface cleaning and sanitization. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
